cap: CIN is graded by how far atypical basal-type cells extend up the epithelium: the lower third in CIN 1, the lower two-thirds in CIN 2, and more than two-thirds up to full thickness in CIN 3, which includes carcinoma in situ. The two-tier terms group CIN 1 as LSIL and CIN 2 or 3 as HSIL. Only a breach of the basement membrane makes the lesion invasive carcinoma.
teach: Read the figure left to right as the same epithelium at five stages. In CIN 1, immature cells fill only the lower third and the upper layers still mature, so the viral effect shows as koilocytes near the surface. In CIN 2 the atypical cells reach two-thirds of the thickness, and in CIN 3 nothing matures, which is carcinoma in situ. None of these breaches the basement membrane, so none can metastasize; invasion begins only when nests cross it. Cytology reports the same spectrum as LSIL (CIN 1) and HSIL (CIN 2 or 3), and diffuse p16 staining settles an equivocal CIN 2 as HSIL. Management follows the grade: surveillance for CIN 1, excision for CIN 2 or 3, and staging for invasion.
